scenarios.key_insight: In an open system reaction (e.g., Metal + Water -> Hydroxide + Hydrogen gas), the mass loss is fixed *per mole of metal*. However, the *percentage* mass loss depends on the Atomic Mass of the metal. A heavier metal (K) producing the same amount of gas (1 mol H2 per 2 mol M) will lose a smaller *fraction* of its mass compared to a lighter metal (Li), or conversely, contribute more mass to the product. Q3 requires analyzing the mass of Oxygen retained vs Hydrogen lost relative to the initial mass added.
discrimination_factors: Relative Atomic Mass trends (Li=7 vs K=39)

scenarios.key_insight: Standard Group 2 trend: Solubility of hydroxides increases down the group (Mg low, Ba high). Standard Group 2 trend: Solubility of sulfates *decreases* down the group. Questions may rely on inverting the expected trend (e.g., 'Which is the most soluble sulfate?' -> Mg). In Q4, recognizing that 'X must be Ba' relies on knowing the Hydroxide trend is opposite to the Sulfate trend.
discrimination_factors: Memorizing opposing trends for different salts (Hydroxides vs Sulfates)
Applying qualitative rules to quantitative titration data

scenarios.key_insight: Reacting a Halogen (Cl2) with a Halide solution (Br-). If Cl2 is more reactive, it becomes Cl- and forces Br- to become Br2. This 'Swap' logic creates a colored solution (Brown/Orange for Br2). Failing this usually stems from treating the periodic table as a layout rather than a reactivity ladder.
discrimination_factors: Internalizing Group 17 reactivity decreases down group
Deducing physical state (color) from reaction outcome
